channel.title: Post-Match Plots
channel.description: Football, drawn with data. One question at a time, answered with charts.

item.title: Is Kobbie Mainoo the one thing going right?
item.description: Kobbie Mainoo is the most accurate passer and best dribbler among the Premier League's central midfielders, and United play better with him. The one gap: he barely shoots or creates.

item.title: So where should United actually be?
item.description: Replay every match from its chances and Manchester United should have 13 points, not 8. Where the points went, and why that only gets them to 15th.

item.title: Is Bruno Fernandes getting worse?
item.description: Bruno Fernandes is creating far fewer chances than last season and shooting more. Here's how much is decline and how much was a freak season.

item.title: How much are set pieces costing United?
item.description: Manchester United have the worst set-piece record in the Premier League: one scored, seven conceded. Here's what it's costing them.

item.title: Why do United concede so many goals from so few shots?
item.description: Manchester United face an average number of shots but concede the best chances in the Premier League. Here's where they come from.

item.title: Are United unlucky in front of goal?
item.description: Manchester United have scored about four goals fewer than their xG. Here's whether that's bad luck or bad finishing.

item.title: Why don't United's 203 shots add up to more?
item.description: United take more shots than any Premier League team, but nearly half come from outside the box and the average one is worth the least.
